title: Microsoft 365 Tenant Decommission & Retirement (Post-Migration)
author_notes: Effort tier: T3 (enterprise Google Cloud / identity / Gemini enablement).

Google Cloud Console / gcloud / Cloud Identity / Google Admin authored at exact detail from Google public docs; version- or preview-dependent capabilities (SCC tiers, BeyondCorp features, org-policy constraints, VPC-SC behaviors, Gemini Enterprise features) cited or flagged 'verify in your organization', never invented. IaC (Terraform / Cloud Foundation Toolkit) at the pattern level. Automation is Python (gcloud / Cloud Client Libraries) — no hardcoded credentials, no committed service-account keys, no secrets in code. No client names.
hook: Cleanly retire the Microsoft 365 tenant after the move to Google
problem: Once users are live on Google Workspace, the old Microsoft 365 tenant is cost, risk, and orphaned data — but pulling the plug carelessly loses records or breaks lingering integrations. This solution is the decommission & retirement runbook: verify migration completeness, handle data disposition and legal-hold/eDiscovery obligations, wind down licensing and Entra app registrations, re-point or remove DNS/integrations, and formally close the tenant — a clean, auditable exit.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the retirement model: completeness verification, data disposition vs retention/legal hold, licensing wind-down, identity/app cleanup, DNS/integration cutover, and formal closure.
Requirements Guide — each prerequisite with how to verify/implement (migration signed off, M365/Entra admin access, legal/records stakeholders, DNS control).

Implementation Guide — verify completeness, export/dispose data under the retention policy, decommission licensing + Entra app registrations, re-point/remove DNS + integrations, and execute formal tenant closure — staged with rollback windows.

5 Python tools — assessment/discovery, a configuration or provisioning helper, a validation/report generator, a policy/guardrail check, and a scope/config helper — authentic gcloud / Cloud Client Library automation (read-only or dry-run by default; no credentials or keys in code).
Validation gates (nothing orphaned, obligations met, closure evidenced) plus Best Practices for a clean, auditable exit; legal-hold determinations deferred to legal/records.
short: Cleanly retire the old Microsoft 365 tenant after the Google move — completeness verification, data disposition + legal-hold handling, licensing wind-down, identity/app cleanup, DNS/integration cutover, and formal closure — an auditable exit. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.

bottom_line: The retired Microsoft 365 tenant closed cleanly and auditably — nothing orphaned, records obligations met, licensing and identity wound down — the cost and risk gone for good.
